title: Credit smoothing window and inactive-user reactivation flow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Seed experiments over the last 12 months show that crisp credit expiry dates drive immediate engagement but also create a sharp dropoff for low-velocity users who would otherwise convert if given more time. We believe a blended approach — a short 'smoothing window' around expiry plus a staged reactivation nudging flow — will (1) reduce churn from the free tier, (2) increase upgrade conversions from dormant users, and (3) keep total credit cost within acceptable guardrails for hosted customers.

Hypothesis: Introducing a 7-day credit smoothing window (soft expiry) and a multi-touch reactivation sequence (in-app banner, follow-up email, time-limited credit boost) will increase 30-day PLG conversion rate for low-activity cohorts by >=15% without increasing fraudulent or wasteful usage by more than 5% of baseline.

Experiment design: Target cohort: free-tier/new-trial users who have used <20% of allocated credits and had no app activity in the prior 14 days. Randomize users into three buckets: control (current expirations/UX), Variant A (7-day smoothing window + in-app banner at t0), Variant B (7-day smoothing + in-app banner + two emails at t+2d and t+5d + 10% temporary credit top-up on click), Variant C (credit top-up only). Implementation notes: smoothing window means credits are still redeemable but flagged; output prompts show 'soft expiry' messaging and remaining-savings meter.

Metrics and instrumentation: Primary metrics: 30-day upgrade conversion rate (free->paid), 30/90-day active user retention, credits burned per user, per-cohort cost uplift. Secondary metrics: CTA click-through rate on nudge banners/emails, support tickets referencing credit confusion, signal of abuse (multiple accounts from same billing fingerprint). Events to instrument: "credit_soft_grace_started", "reactivation_banner_shown", "reactivation_email_sent", "reactivation_email_clicked", "reactivation_credit_awarded", "upgrade_cta_clicked", "credits_consumed_snapshot".

Success criteria: win if Variant B increases 30-day conversion by >=15% (relative to control) while credits cost uplift <=5% and fraud signals unchanged. Preserve NPS trend (no negative lift in support sentiment).

Rollout plan: feature-flagged server-side rollout behind a PLG experiment switch. Phase 1 (week 0-2): small internal/employee canary + QA. Phase 2 (week 2-4): 5% of eligible live cohort. Phase 3 (week 4-8): ramp to 25% then full 100% if metrics hold. Monitoring: daily dashboards, alert if daily credit cost variance >2x expected or if conversion delta is negative beyond -5%.

Org impact and cross-functional asks: Engineering (backend + billing + notifications) to add smoothing window expiry state and ops endpoints; Analytics to build cohort queries and dashboards; Growth to own copy and email cadence; Legal to review T&Cs/enterprise contract language re: credit carryover and promotional credits; Security & Compliance to run quick review ensuring the top-up flow cannot be gamed.

Risks and mitigations: Risk of users creating multiple accounts to harvest temporary top-ups -> mitigate with billing fingerprint heuristics and short-lived boost. Risk of enterprise confusion -> add clear contract clause and admin opt-out for enterprise customers.

Notes on enterprise SQ: this change affects wording in the security questionnaire and contract FAQ (credit expiration policy). Proposed contract change: add an appendix clarifying promotional / grace-period credits are marketing promotions and not billable credits for committed capacity customers; provide an opt-out flag for Dedicated/Private customers.

Next steps: finalize copy + email templates, engineering scoping (ENG ticket), analytics event contract, legal review by end of cycle.
